title: Whose song is it anyway?
summary_es: Pódcast: una presentadora escéptica entrevista a un compositor que usa inteligencia artificial sobre quién es el autor de esa música.
prediction_prompt: If you ask a program for fifty melodies and choose one, have you written it? Where would you draw the line?

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: This week we're asking an awkward question: if a machine writes a song, whose song is it?

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: With me is Owen Hart, a composer who's been using these tools since before they were fashionable.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Owen, let's start with a confession. How much of your last album did you actually write?

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Ha. Depends what you mean by write. I'd say all of it, and my lawyer would agree.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: But I'd be lying if I claimed every note came out of my own head.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: So where did the rest come from?

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: I'd feed the system a rough idea, say eight bars, and ask for fifty variations.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Forty-eight of them were garbage. One was fine. And one was something I'd never have thought of.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: And that one ended up on the record.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: It did. Though by the time I'd finished with it, you'd hardly have recognised it.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: That sounds suspiciously like what people say when they've copied someone's homework.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Fair enough. But think about how composers have always worked.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: You sit at a piano and your hands fall into patterns you learned from other people.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Nobody accuses a pianist of stealing from their teacher. We call it influence, or tradition.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: There's a difference, though, isn't there? Your teacher agreed to teach you.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: The musicians whose recordings trained these systems were never asked, let alone paid.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: No, and I think that's indefensible. I'm not going to pretend otherwise.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: If I had my way, there'd be a licence, the way radio stations pay to play records.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: The companies would say that's unworkable. Millions of tracks, millions of rights holders.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: They said the same about streaming, and somehow the accountants managed.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: It's remarkable how solvable a problem becomes once someone's obliged to solve it.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: You sound almost optimistic.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Cautiously. I've been in this business long enough to know that musicians are usually paid last.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Let me push you on authorship. Suppose I type 'sad song, piano, rainy evening' and press a button.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Have I composed something?

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: I'd say you've commissioned something. Which isn't nothing, but it isn't composing either.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: The interesting work starts afterwards, when you decide what to keep and what to throw away.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: So taste is the last thing left to us.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Taste, and stubbornness. A machine will give you a hundred answers without caring about any of them.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: A person keeps going until one of them feels true. That's the part I can't delegate.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Isn't that a rather romantic way of describing what is, after all, a selection process?

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Possibly. But editing has always been the unglamorous half of making anything worth hearing.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Do you worry that listeners won't care? That good enough will simply be good enough?

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: For background music, honestly, that ship has sailed. Nobody's hiring a quartet for a shampoo advert.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: But people don't queue in the rain to hear something merely competent.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: They go because another human being stood up and meant it.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: You can't fake that, at least not yet, and I rather hope not ever.

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: That's either very wise or very convenient for a man with an album to sell.

segments.speaker: owen
segments.text: Can't it be both?

segments.speaker: ruth
segments.text: Owen Hart, thank you. The album, written by him, more or less, is out now.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *have* se queda en /əv/ y *thought of* se enlaza, con la *t* suavizada en americano: suena «zórav».
*you'd* (= you would) apenas se oye, y *have* vuelve a reducirse a /əv/. Si pierdes las dos, la frase parece decir «you hardly recognised it».
*let alone* se dice como una sola palabra, con el acento en *-lone*.
La *t* final de *isn't* desaparece delante de consonante, y *but it* se funde en /bəɾɪɾ/.
*has* se reduce a /əz/ y se pega a *ship*: «shípaz». La *t* de *that* se corta en la garganta.

tasks.prompt: What is the conversation mainly about?

options.text: How to make a living as a professional pianist these days
Who can claim authorship of AI-assisted music
Why streaming services pay artists so little
How recording technology has changed since the radio age

tasks.rationale_es: Ruth lo plantea en la primera frase (si una máquina escribe una canción, ¿de quién es?) y vuelve a ello cuando «aprieta» a Owen sobre la autoría.

tasks.prompt: Which best describes the host's manner towards her guest?

options.text: Openly hostile throughout the whole conversation
Uncritically admiring
Bored and distracted
Sceptical but good-humoured

tasks.rationale_es: Le pincha con ironía (lo de «copiar los deberes», lo de que su postura es «muy conveniente»), pero en tono de broma y dejándole responder.

tasks.prompt: How did Owen use the system when making his album?

options.text: He requested many versions of a short idea and kept very few
He let it produce complete songs, which he then released under his own name
He used it only to check his finished work for mistakes
He trained it on recordings of his own piano playing

tasks.rationale_es: Le daba unos ocho compases y pedía cincuenta variaciones; cuarenta y ocho eran basura, una pasable y otra, una sorpresa.

tasks.prompt: What does the host imply with her remark about copied homework?

options.text: That Owen was a poor student at music school
That she herself has been accused of copying in the past
That Owen's explanation sounds like an excuse
That the software was built by students

tasks.rationale_es: Owen acaba de decir que lo cambió tanto que no se reconocería, y ella responde que eso es lo que dice quien ha copiado: pone en duda su justificación.

tasks.prompt: What is Owen's view of how these systems were trained?

options.text: It is no different from learning from a teacher
It is regrettable, but nothing can realistically be done about it now
It is a matter for lawyers, not for musicians
It was wrong, and creators ought to be paid

tasks.rationale_es: Dice que es *indefensible* y propone una licencia, como la que pagan las emisoras de radio.

tasks.prompt: Why does Owen bring up streaming?

options.text: To show that the industry solves hard problems when it has to
To complain about how little he earns from it
To argue that a licensing scheme would be too expensive to administer
To explain how his album is distributed

tasks.rationale_es: Las empresas dicen que licenciar millones de pistas es inviable; él recuerda que dijeron lo mismo del *streaming* y que «los contables se las arreglaron».

tasks.prompt: Owen believes that typing a description and pressing a button counts as composing.
tasks.rationale_es: Para él eso es *commissioning* (encargar): «no es poca cosa, pero tampoco es componer».

tasks.prompt: According to Owen, what can a person do that the machine cannot?

options.text: Produce a large number of ideas in a very short space of time
Play an instrument in front of an audience
Persist until a result seems genuinely right
Remember what earlier composers wrote

tasks.rationale_es: La máquina da cien respuestas sin que le importe ninguna; la persona sigue hasta que una *feels true*. Eso es lo que no puede delegar.

tasks.prompt: Owen thinks AI has already won the market for background music.
tasks.rationale_es: *That ship has sailed*: da esa batalla por perdida. Nadie contrata a un cuarteto para un anuncio de champú.

tasks.prompt: What does Owen mean by "that ship has sailed"?

options.text: The business is growing fast
It is too late to change it
The work has moved abroad to countries where costs are lower
Nobody knows what will happen

tasks.rationale_es: Modismo: el barco ya ha zarpado, es decir, la oportunidad de evitarlo ya pasó.

tasks.prompt: Owen's new album has sold more copies than his previous one.
tasks.rationale_es: Solo se dice que el álbum ya está a la venta; no se habla de cifras.

tasks.prompt: What is the tone of the host's final comment about the album?

options.text: Gently ironic
Deeply impressed by what she has just heard
Openly dismissive
Apologetic

tasks.rationale_es: *written by him, more or less*: retoma con una sonrisa la pregunta de toda la entrevista sobre cuánto escribió él en realidad.

tasks.reference: It did. Though by the time I'd finished with it, you'd hardly have recognised it.
accept_variants: It did. Though by the time I had finished with it, you would hardly have recognised it.
tasks.rationale_es: Dos contracciones con *'d* de valor distinto: *I'd finished* (had) y *you'd… have* (would).

tasks.reference: I'd say you've commissioned something. Which isn't nothing, but it isn't composing either.
tasks.rationale_es: *isn't* pierde la *t* y *but it* se funde. Fíjate en la doble negación deliberada: *isn't nothing*.

tasks.reference: For background music, honestly, that ship has sailed. Nobody's hiring a quartet for a shampoo advert.
tasks.rationale_es: *has* reducido tras *ship* y la contracción *Nobody's* (= nobody is).
